mined_rules.label: CONFIRMED
mined_rules.why: AGENTS.md states the requirement verbatim; only the mined detail that `MagicMock(autospec=True)` is a silently-ignored keyword is undocumented.
mined_rules.rule: Mocks standing in for a real Airflow, provider or SDK type must be specced - MagicMock(spec=...), spec_set= or create_autospec, including nested attributes - so signature drift against the real class fails the test; MagicMock(autospec=True) is a no-op keyword and specs nothing.

mined_rules.label: CONFIRMED
mined_rules.doc_reference: AGENTS.md § Coding Standards — "Imports at top of file. Valid exceptions: circular imports, lazy loading for worker isolation, `TYPE_CHECKING` blocks."
mined_rules.why: The rule and its exception list are stated almost word for word; only the mined addition that the exception must carry a comment naming the reason is absent from the docs.
mined_rules.rule: Put imports at module scope; an import inside a function, method, fixture or test body is acceptable only to break a genuine circular import or for deliberate lazy loading (worker isolation, `TYPE_CHECKING`), and must carry a comment naming the reason — stdlib modules always go at the top of the file.

mined_rules.label: CONFIRMED
mined_rules.doc_reference: AGENTS.md § Naming — "Write **Dag** (title case) in all prose. Keep the all-caps or lowercase spelling only when reproducing a literal code token"
mined_rules.why: The Dag/DAG spelling requirement and the code-identifier carve-out are stated explicitly; the mined rule's extra targets ("webserver", "DAG processor", "API Server") are not named in the docs but ride on the same requirement.
mined_rules.rule: In user-facing prose - documentation, newsfragments, release notes, changelog entries, config.yml descriptions and UI strings - spell Airflow's core nouns the Airflow 3 way (Dag, Dags, Dag run, Dag files, Dag bundles, Dag Processor, API Server); never all-caps DAG/DAGs, "DAG processor" or "webserver", and reserve all-caps DAG for code identifiers and quoted strings.

mined_rules.label: IMPLIED
mined_rules.doc_reference: contributing-docs/13_airflow_dependencies_and_extras.rst § Referring to other Apache Airflow distributions in dependencies — "Some of our dependencies have forced minimum version - mostly because of the Airflow 3 minimum version compatibility"; contributing-docs/12_provider_distributions.rst § Breaking changes in the community managed providers — "All providers are in theory backward compatible with future versions of Airflow"
mined_rules.why: The docs establish that a provider declares and must honour a minimum supported Airflow version, but they discuss this only as a dependency floor and never state the code-level requirement to gate a newer core symbol behind an `AIRFLOW_V_X_Y_PLUS` check or a `getattr` fallback.
mined_rules.rule: A provider must not unconditionally import, call or attribute-access an airflow-core symbol that does not exist in its minimum supported core version: gate it behind an AIRFLOW_V_X_Y_PLUS check (or `getattr(obj, "attr", default)`) and keep the older fallback path.

mined_rules.label: TRIBAL
mined_rules.why: contributing-docs/16_adding_api_endpoints.rst is the only doc covering FastAPI endpoints and it never mentions the datamodels, services or Query* filter modules — its "Optional: Adding Pydantic Model" step says only that you "may define a model in a Python file".
mined_rules.rule: Keep FastAPI route modules to route handlers only: Pydantic request/response models belong in the package's datamodels module, authorization and business helpers in its services module, query/filter construction in the corresponding Query* filter class's to_orm, and callback or domain-object definitions in the module that owns the domain model.

mined_rules.label: CONFIRMED
mined_rules.doc_reference: contributing-docs/05_pull_requests.rst § Pull Request quality criteria, item 6 "Coherent changes" (plus the earlier bullet "Make sure your PR is small and focused on one change only - avoid adding unrelated changes") and § Gen-AI Assisted contributions
mined_rules.why: Keeping the diff to what the PR claims is stated as a quality criterion PRs are measured against, and AGENTS.md's self-review step 1 repeats it; the uv.lock and split-migration specifics are the mined refinement.
mined_rules.rule: Keep a PR's diff scoped to what its title and description claim: regenerate uv.lock against fresh main so it carries only the dependency changes this PR actually makes, and split an independent schema-fix migration or a second unrelated feature into its own PR or call it out in the description with its own rationale.

mined_rules.label: TRIBAL
mined_rules.why: Nothing in AGENTS.md or contributing-docs describes deferrable-operator event handling, `execute_complete`, or the statuses a trigger may emit.
mined_rules.rule: In `execute_complete`, branch explicitly on `event["status"]` and handle every status the paired trigger can emit — success, error, timeout and cancelled — before reading any payload field; never collapse all non-success statuses into one failure branch.

mined_rules.label: TRIBAL
mined_rules.why: No document discusses truthiness versus explicit `is not None` / `!== undefined` presence checks in either Python or TypeScript.
mined_rules.rule: Test for presence with an explicit `is not None` (Python) or `!== undefined && !== null` (TypeScript) rather than truthiness wherever `0`, `False` or an empty string is a legitimate value.

mined_rules.label: IMPLIED
mined_rules.doc_reference: contributing-docs/05_pull_requests.rst — "If your PR adds functionality, make sure to update the docs as part of the same PR, not only code and tests. Docstring is often sufficient."; AGENTS.md § Coding Standards — "Keep selective-checks behaviour and its documentation in sync"
mined_rules.why: The docs require documentation to be updated alongside code and give one worked instance of a doc/behaviour sync obligation, but never state that a `:param:` docstring's override/fallback/validation semantics must match what the implementation actually does.
mined_rules.rule: A parameter's documented semantics must match what the code actually does with it: whether the value overrides, is appended to or merged with an underlying default; what the real fallback is when it is unset; and how much the code actually validates. Fix whichever side is wrong - reword the docstring, or make the implementation pass the value conditionally so the documented fallback really applies

mined_rules.label: TRIBAL
mined_rules.why: contributing-docs/09_testing.rst only enumerates the kinds of tests Airflow has; no fetched document mentions Playwright, e2e specs, page objects or assertion style (the contributing-docs/testing/ sub-pages are not in this corpus).
mined_rules.rule: E2e tests and page objects must fail when the feature is broken: no if-guards around the assertions and no try/catch or .catch(() => false) around visibility/state checks - use web-first assertions such as expect(el).toBeVisible()/toBeHidden() and let failures propagate.

mined_rules.label: TRIBAL
mined_rules.why: contributing-docs/16_adding_api_endpoints.rst tells you to register the route with "the appropriate HTTP method, query params, permissions, body type" and to check the auto-generated /docs, but never mentions the `responses=` mapping or agreement between declared and returned status codes.
mined_rules.rule: A FastAPI route decorator must declare every status code its handler can produce: each status raised via HTTPException belongs in the responses= mapping, and the decorator's status_code must agree with the success codes the handler actually returns.

mined_rules.label: IMPLIED
mined_rules.doc_reference: contributing-docs/12_provider_distributions.rst § Breaking changes in the community managed providers — "Ideally you should provide a migration path for the users to follow in the ``changelog.rst``"
mined_rules.why: The docs treat changes to a provider's public surface as breaking changes that must be communicated and given a migration path, but explicitly allow them; they never require the change to be made opt-in behind a new parameter defaulting to the legacy behaviour.
mined_rules.rule: Keep the public surface of provider operators, hooks and extractors backward compatible: a changed return value, changed traversal, or new constructor keyword must be opt-in via a new parameter defaulting to the legacy behaviour, and existing public signatures (e.g. `BaseExtractor.__init__(self, operator)`) must keep working.

mined_rules.label: CONFIRMED
mined_rules.doc_reference: AGENTS.md § Boundaries — "**Never** ... Edit generated files by hand when a generation workflow exists." (echoed by contributing-docs/15_node_environment_setup.rst on ``/openapi-gen``: "autogenerated types and queries ... Do not manually edit.")
mined_rules.why: The general prohibition is stated as an absolute; the mined rule only adds which two files are generated and by which command.
mined_rules.rule: Never hand-edit generated files; change the source of truth and regenerate in the same commit - `get_provider_info.py` comes from `provider.yaml` via `prek run update-providers-build-files`, and the task-SDK `datamodels/_generated.py` comes from the Execution API OpenAPI schema

mined_rules.label: CONFIRMED
mined_rules.doc_reference: AGENTS.md § Coding Standards, newsfragments bullet — "**Golden rule: never create a newsfragment unless you are certain the change is user-facing.** ... Adding a spurious newsfragment for a non-user-facing change is a defect, not a safe default." (repeated in § Commits and PRs)
mined_rules.why: The "no newsfragment for a docs-only or purely internal change" half is stated outright; the bugfix-versus-significant type choice is only gestured at by the type list in contributing-docs/18_contribution_workflow.rst.
mined_rules.rule: Pick the newsfragment from the change's actual user-visible impact: none at all for a documentation-only or purely internal change, and bugfix.rst rather than significant.rst for an internal fix that changes no observable behaviour.

mined_rules.label: TRIBAL
mined_rules.why: No document states where instance attributes must be initialised or forbids first-assigning `self.<attr>` in `execute()`/`run()`/`get_conn()`.
mined_rules.rule: Instance attributes belong to `__init__`: initialise every resource handle and state flag there, and never first-assign or overwrite them in `execute()`, `run()`, `submit()` or `get_conn()` — those methods resolve values into local variables and reset released resources to `None` after cleanup.

mined_rules.label: TRIBAL
mined_rules.why: Not merely undocumented but documented backwards: AGENTS.md § Coding Standards forbids adding new `raise AirflowException(...)` anywhere including `providers`, while review history requires exactly that on operator/trigger failure and timeout branches.
mined_rules.rule: Operator, sensor and trigger error paths — including the failure and timeout branches of `execute_complete` — must raise Airflow exception types (`AirflowException`, `AirflowFailException`, `AirflowTaskTimeout`), never `RuntimeError` or another builtin.

mined_rules.label: TRIBAL
mined_rules.why: No document discusses cleanup placement, `try/finally` coverage of early-exit guards, or post-submit commands.
mined_rules.rule: Post-submit commands and other cleanup that must run once a job finishes belong in a `try/finally` that covers the whole method including its early-exit guards, so they execute on success, failure and kill alike.

mined_rules.label: IMPLIED
mined_rules.doc_reference: contributing-docs/12_provider_distributions.rst § Breaking changes in the community managed providers — "You have to update ``changelog.rst`` file in the ``docs`` folder ... If in doubt, you can always look at ``changelog.rst`` in other providers to see how we communicate"
mined_rules.why: The docs point at existing changelogs as the style model rather than stating the style, and AGENTS.md's ban on Conventional-Commit prefixes is scoped to commit messages and PR titles, not changelog lines.
mined_rules.rule: Provider changelog.rst entries must read as sentence-case, user-facing prose: strip conventional-commit prefixes such as fix: or feat(...), do not open with a lowercase word, name no internal tooling such as Dependabot, and state the concrete change.

mined_rules.label: TRIBAL
mined_rules.why: AGENTS.md's only naming requirements are Dag capitalisation and action-verb function names; nothing tells a contributor to reuse Airflow's established term for a concept (`run_after`, `wait_for_completion`, the `a`-prefixed async variant).
mined_rules.rule: Reuse Airflow's established name for a concept instead of inventing a synonym: `run_after` for the DAG run scheduling timestamp, `wait_for_completion` for the wait-for-finish flag, and an `a`-prefixed method name (`aget_connection`) for the async variant of an existing method.

mined_rules.label: TRIBAL
mined_rules.why: AGENTS.md's only database-performance requirement concerns batching bulk DELETE/UPDATE in the scheduler loop; nothing addresses column selection, `load_only()` or narrowing `with_row_locks` selects.
mined_rules.rule: Fetch exactly the columns the consuming code reads: enumerate columns instead of select(SomeModel) in grid/UI and other hot-path queries, restrict with_row_locks selects to the key actually used, and do not add a column to load_only() that no caller consumes.

mined_rules.label: IMPLIED
mined_rules.doc_reference: contributing-docs/13_airflow_dependencies_and_extras.rst § Referring to other Apache Airflow distributions in dependencies — the ``common.compat`` guidance: "because it is one that changes often and almost always when it changes, there are some providers that need those changes"
mined_rules.why: The docs treat `common.compat` as the shared package providers depend on for cross-version needs, but frame it purely as a dependency-versioning concern and never say to prefer it over inline `packaging.version.parse` comparisons or per-provider copies.
mined_rules.rule: Express cross-version Airflow compatibility through the shared compat layer — the `AIRFLOW_V_X_Y_PLUS` sentinels in `version_compat` and the helpers in `providers/common/compat` — instead of inline `packaging.version.parse` comparisons or per-provider copies of the same check.

mined_rules.label: TRIBAL
mined_rules.why: No document mentions `AirflowOptionalProviderFeatureException` or an import guard; the nearest text (contributing-docs/12_provider_distributions.rst, optional-extras Shape B, step 4) assumes the opposite — an unguarded module-level `from <module> import ...` made to work in CI by injecting `sys.modules[...] = MagicMock()` in conftest.
mined_rules.rule: Import anything a provider does not require unconditionally — a package behind an optional extra, or another provider's package — inside `try`/`except ImportError`, and either raise `AirflowOptionalProviderFeatureException` naming the extra to install or degrade the feature; never import it unconditionally at module top level.

mined_rules.label: CONFIRMED
mined_rules.doc_reference: AGENTS.md § Coding Standards — "Never add new direct `raise AirflowException(...)` usages ... the `check-no-new-airflow-exceptions` prek hook enforces this across `airflow-core`, `airflow-ctl`, `task-sdk`, `providers`, and `shared`. Prefer a Python built-in (`ValueError`, `TypeError`, `OSError`, …)"
mined_rules.why: Stated as an absolute with the same preferred alternatives the mined rule names, and explicitly scoped to `providers`.
mined_rules.rule: In provider code, raise the most appropriate built-in Python exception (ValueError, TypeError, RuntimeError) for argument validation, internal invariant violations and third-party service failures, rather than AirflowException.

mined_rules.label: IMPLIED
mined_rules.doc_reference: contributing-docs/12_provider_distributions.rst § Breaking changes in the community managed providers — "When you introduce a breaking change in the provider, you have to make sure that you communicate it properly ... Ideally you should provide a migration path"
mined_rules.why: The docs require communication and a migration path for provider breaking changes but never require the deprecated forwarding property or the parameter-value mapping that the review history demands instead of a clean removal.
mined_rules.rule: Public provider API must stay backward compatible: renaming an executor attribute or method requires a deprecated property/forwarding wrapper under the old name, and removing an operator parameter requires deprecating it and mapping its values onto the replacement rather than dropping it.

mined_rules.label: IMPLIED
mined_rules.doc_reference: AGENTS.md § Testing Standards — "Do not assert on raw log text (`caplog.text` for example), these are legacy string matching APIs planned for removal. Structured assertions via `caplog` ... are fine and preferred"
mined_rules.why: The docs forbid only raw-text `caplog` assertions and explicitly bless structured `caplog` assertions, so they stop short of the mined rule's broader "do not use the caplog fixture to assert on log output at all".
mined_rules.rule: Do not use pytest's caplog fixture to assert on log output; assert on observable behaviour or return values, or capture the logger directly with a mock.

mined_rules.label: TRIBAL
mined_rules.why: No fetched document mentions Playwright, navigation helpers, `expect.poll()` or `waitForLoadState`.
mined_rules.rule: In Playwright e2e tests, wait on an explicit UI condition - a key element becoming visible before a navigation helper returns, expect.poll() for post-click assertions - never read state immediately after an action and never page.waitForLoadState('networkidle').

their_rules.statement: Write Dag (title case) in all prose; keep the all-caps or lowercase spelling only when reproducing a literal code token (the `DAG` SDK class, `dag_id`, CLI commands, paths and config keys, anti-pattern quotes).
their_rules.label: SUPPORTED
their_rules.why: The strongest docs-side match in the corpus: six PRs of review comments correcting DAG/Dag spelling in newsfragments, release notes, config descriptions and translated UI strings, plus below-threshold candidate airflow-r708 (support 1) extending it to docstrings and test names.

their_rules.statement: Do not spell out "Directed Acyclic Graph" except for historical context.
their_rules.label: UNSUPPORTED
their_rules.why: No mined rule and no below-threshold candidate touches the expanded phrase; this looks like a convention nobody violates — contributors write "Dag", not the expansion — rather than one tooling suppresses.

their_rules.statement: The Scheduler reads serialized Dags and never runs user code.
their_rules.label: UNSUPPORTED
their_rules.why: No mined rule; the nearest candidate (airflow-r664, support 1) polices architecture *documentation* asserting this, not code violating it — evidence that the boundary is structural enough that diffs never breach it, so reviewers only ever argue about how it is described.

their_rules.statement: Workers execute tasks via the Task SDK and communicate through the Execution API — never accessing the metadata DB directly.
their_rules.label: UNSUPPORTED
their_rules.why: No evidence because software guards enforce it before review: AGENTS.md itself says guards steer these processes through the Execution API. The corpus polices the adjacent seam instead — candidate airflow-r532 (support 2) on airflow-core importing task-SDK internals, and airflow-r555 (support 1) on unread fields in execution-API worker context models.

their_rules.statement: Each distribution must declare the other distributions it needs, so `uv --project <FOLDER> sync` installs only that project's dependencies.
their_rules.label: SUPPORTED
their_rules.why: Relied on .bob/rules/airflow-candidates.md: airflow-r745 (support 2, below the promotion threshold) requires every package a provider imports directly to be declared in that provider's pyproject.toml in the same PR — the same expectation, at provider granularity.

their_rules.statement: Always format and check every Python file you create or modify with `uv run ruff format <file>` and `uv run ruff check --fix <file>` before moving on.
their_rules.label: UNSUPPORTED
their_rules.why: No evidence because tooling catches it first — the ruff and ruff-format prek hooks run pre-commit and in CI, so a formatting violation never reaches a human reviewer's line comment.

their_rules.statement: No `assert` in production code.
their_rules.label: UNSUPPORTED
their_rules.why: No evidence because tooling catches it first (ruff's assert rules run in the static-check hooks). The only assert-related candidate, airflow-r610 (support 1), recommends `if TYPE_CHECKING: assert x is not None` for type narrowing — a runtime no-op, so not a counter-example.

their_rules.statement: Comment sparingly — code says what, comments say why; no narrating comments that restate the next line, no multi-line prose padding, no repeating the same rationale at several sites.
their_rules.label: UNSUPPORTED
their_rules.why: No mined rule asks for fewer comments. Notably, every comment-related candidate pushes the other way in scope but not in spirit — airflow-r618, r202, r702, r195, r579, r040 all demand an explanatory comment at a genuinely non-obvious site, which is precisely the carve-out this rule grants; reviewers evidently police missing why-comments, not excess what-comments.

their_rules.statement: Use `time.monotonic()` for durations, not `time.time()`.
their_rules.label: SUPPORTED
their_rules.why: Relied on .bob/rules/airflow-candidates.md: airflow-r521 states the rule for triggers and operators and airflow-r515 requires tests to use the same clock as the implementation — but both sit at support 1, so the review history confirms the rule only weakly.

their_rules.statement: In `airflow-core`, functions with a `session` parameter must not call `session.commit()`, and `session` parameters must be keyword-only.
their_rules.label: SUPPORTED
their_rules.why: Relied on .bob/rules/airflow-candidates.md: airflow-r638 (keep commit responsibility in one place — a caller must not commit when its helper already does) and airflow-r646 (use `session.flush()` inside a method participating in a larger transaction) both express the no-commit half, each at support 1; the keyword-only half drew no comments at all.

their_rules.statement: Imports at top of file. Valid exceptions: circular imports, lazy loading for worker isolation, `TYPE_CHECKING` blocks.
their_rules.label: SUPPORTED
their_rules.why: Six PRs of review comments on function-local imports, matching the doc's exception list; the review history adds one requirement the doc lacks — the exception must carry a comment naming the cycle or lazy-loading reason (see also candidate airflow-r579, support 1).

their_rules.statement: Guard heavy type-only imports (e.g. `kubernetes.client`) with `TYPE_CHECKING` in multi-process code paths.
their_rules.label: UNSUPPORTED
their_rules.why: No mined rule expresses the import-weight concern. The two TYPE_CHECKING candidates are about something else — airflow-r752 (which module to import `Context` from) and airflow-r018 (annotating as `SerializedDAG`) — so the corpus cannot tell us whether the rule is obeyed or simply never comes up.

their_rules.statement: Never add new direct `raise AirflowException(...)` usages; prefer a Python built-in (`ValueError`, `TypeError`, `OSError`) or a dedicated class in the appropriate `exceptions.py`, and narrow existing ones when you touch them.
their_rules.label: CONTRADICTED
their_rules.why: The review history is split by surface: airflow-r436 (support 3, #62240/#60963/#55068) confirms the rule for provider argument validation, invariant violations and third-party failures, but airflow-r425 (support 3, #64119/#64051/#56936) pushes the other way on operator, sensor and trigger error paths, where reviewers required `AirflowException`/`AirflowFailException`/`AirflowTaskTimeout` and rejected `RuntimeError` — the AGENTS.md wording admits no such carve-out, and candidate airflow-r138 (support 1) adds a third answer (`SystemExit` for provider CLI config errors).

their_rules.statement: Translate domain-layer exceptions to `HTTPException` at FastAPI route boundaries — catch `ValueError` and similar from domain code and re-raise as 404 for not-found, 400 for invalid input, so they do not propagate as 500.
their_rules.label: UNSUPPORTED
their_rules.why: No mined rule states it. The corpus does police route-boundary error handling but with the opposite emphasis — candidate airflow-r452 (support 1) warns against forwarding arbitrary internal messages as 4xx detail strings, and airflow-r479 (support 1) says the API layer should reject bad input rather than let a model helper raise — so the concern is live, but the specific translate-don't-500 requirement left no trace.

their_rules.statement: Bulk `DELETE`/`UPDATE` in the scheduler loop or any synchronous interval task must be batched with `LIMIT` and committed between batches; filter columns used by the cleanup must be indexed.
their_rules.label: SUPPORTED
their_rules.why: Relied on .bob/rules/airflow-candidates.md: airflow-r630 and airflow-r724 (both support 2) require batching rather than per-row database work, and airflow-r164 (support 1) requires an explicit index on a foreign-key column used as a scheduler subquery filter predicate — together they cover both halves, though none is framed as the scheduler-loop unbounded-write case AGENTS.md describes.

their_rules.statement: Name functions and methods with action verbs (`get_`, `extract_`, `find_`, `compute_`, `build_`); avoid noun-only names like `_serialize_keys`, except `is_`/`has_` predicates.
their_rules.label: UNSUPPORTED
their_rules.why: No evidence despite an unusually rich naming corpus: the candidates file holds roughly twenty naming comments (airflow-r236, r237, r238, r705 through r717, r851 and others) and every one argues about which term to use, never about verb-versus-noun form — which reads as a convention already well obeyed rather than one nobody checks.

their_rules.statement: Apache License header on all new files.
their_rules.label: UNSUPPORTED
their_rules.why: No evidence because tooling catches it first — AGENTS.md says "prek enforces this" and contributing-docs/05_pull_requests.rst says prek adds the header automatically, so a missing header is fixed before a reviewer could comment on it.

their_rules.statement: Keep selective-checks behaviour and its documentation in sync: a change to `dev/breeze/src/airflow_breeze/utils/selective_checks.py` must update `dev/breeze/doc/ci/04_selective_checks.md` and adjust `dev/breeze/tests/test_selective_checks.py` in the same PR.
their_rules.label: UNSUPPORTED
their_rules.why: No mined rule. The corpus does reach into that file — candidate airflow-r355 (support 1) requires specific globs in a `selective_checks.py` file group — but never asks for the accompanying doc or test update, so this is likely a low-traffic rule rather than a well-obeyed or tool-enforced one.

their_rules.statement: Never create a newsfragment unless you are certain the change is user-facing; build/release tooling, CI, packaging, internal refactors and test-only changes get none, and a spurious newsfragment is a defect.
their_rules.source: AGENTS.md § Coding Standards (newsfragments bullet), repeated in § Commits and PRs
their_rules.label: SUPPORTED
their_rules.why: Reviewers removed a newsfragment from a docs-only PR and downgraded significant.rst to bugfix.rst for internal fixes with no observable behaviour change — the same golden rule, plus a type-selection refinement the docs do not state.

their_rules.statement: Never add newsfragments for `providers/` or `airflow-ctl/` — their release managers regenerate the changelog from `git log`; edit `providers/<provider>/docs/changelog.rst` or `airflow-ctl/RELEASE_NOTES.rst` instead.
their_rules.source: AGENTS.md § Coding Standards / § Commits and PRs
their_rules.label: CONTRADICTED
their_rules.why: Relied on .bob/rules/airflow-candidates.md: candidate airflow-r190 records a reviewer requiring a `providers/<pkg>/newsfragments/<pr>.feature.rst` newsfragment when adding deferrable mode to a provider operator — the exact thing this rule forbids. The contradiction rests on a single below-threshold observation (support 1, #63614) and may simply predate the AGENTS.md wording, so it flags a divergence to check rather than a settled counter-convention.

their_rules.statement: For a user-visible note in a provider, edit `providers/<provider>/docs/changelog.rst` directly.
their_rules.label: SUPPORTED
their_rules.why: The mined history not only confirms the changelog is the place but adds what the entry must read like — sentence-case user-facing prose, no `fix:`/`feat:` prefixes, no mention of Dependabot — reinforced by candidates airflow-r663, airflow-r652 and airflow-r527 (support 2, 2 and 1).

their_rules.statement: Target exactly 100% coverage of what the PR changes: every changed or added behaviour must have a test that fails without the change, and no tests for pre-existing logic or for standard-library/third-party functions.
their_rules.label: SUPPORTED
their_rules.why: Relied on .bob/rules/airflow-candidates.md for the first half — airflow-r795 (support 2) requires a test pinning every auth branch added or reordered, airflow-r796 (support 1) a test for every public hook method added, and contributing-docs/09_testing.rst states a PR should have a unit test. The "no more than 100%" half — do not test pre-existing or third-party logic — drew no comments at all, so only half this requirement is evidenced.

their_rules.statement: Use pytest patterns, not `unittest.TestCase`.
their_rules.label: UNSUPPORTED
their_rules.why: No mined rule and no candidate. The repo-wide migration off `unittest.TestCase` is long finished and ruff's pytest-style rules run in the static checks, so this reads as a mix of well-obeyed and tool-enforced rather than unchecked.

their_rules.statement: Use `spec`/`autospec` when mocking.
their_rules.label: SUPPORTED
their_rules.why: The best-supported rule in the whole mined set (support 9), spanning core models, providers and task-SDK tests; review history also adds the trap the doc omits — `MagicMock(autospec=True)` is a no-op keyword that specs nothing.

their_rules.statement: Prefer `@mock.patch` decorators over `with mock.patch(...)` context managers for patching.
their_rules.label: UNSUPPORTED
their_rules.why: No mined rule or candidate distinguishes the decorator from the context-manager form; nothing in the evidence says whether this is obeyed or merely never raised.

their_rules.statement: Use `conf_vars` (from `tests_common.test_utils.config`) for Airflow config overrides — as a decorator when the value is fixed, as a context manager when it varies via parametrize.
their_rules.label: SUPPORTED
their_rules.why: Relied on .bob/rules/airflow-candidates.md: airflow-r805 requires `conf_vars` rather than `unittest.mock.patch` on `conf.get`, and airflow-r810 requires exercising the flag-off state with `conf_vars` — both support 1, so real but thin.

their_rules.statement: Use `time_machine` for time-dependent tests; do not use `datetime.now()`.
their_rules.label: SUPPORTED
their_rules.why: Relied on .bob/rules/airflow-candidates.md: airflow-r332 requires freezing time with `time_machine` rather than deriving expected values from `datetime.now()`/`utcnow()`, and airflow-r299 bans `datetime.now()` in provider code in favour of `timezone.utcnow()`; both support 1, with airflow-r515 on clock consistency alongside.

their_rules.statement: Use `@pytest.mark.parametrize` for multiple similar inputs — consolidate tests that differ only in input/expected values.
their_rules.label: UNSUPPORTED
their_rules.why: No mined rule or candidate asks for consolidation into a parametrized test; the corpus mentions `parametrize` only incidentally (candidate airflow-r717, renaming parametrize ids after a Helm migration), so the evidence cannot say whether the rule is obeyed or unenforced.

their_rules.statement: Use `@pytest.mark.db_test` for tests that require database access.
their_rules.label: UNSUPPORTED
their_rules.why: No evidence because tooling catches it first — Airflow's pytest plugin splits db and non-db runs, so a missing marker fails CI rather than drawing a review comment.

their_rules.statement: Test location mirrors source: `airflow/cli/cli_parser.py` → `tests/cli/test_cli_parser.py`.
their_rules.label: UNSUPPORTED
their_rules.why: No mined rule. Candidate airflow-r528 (support 1) is adjacent — rename the corresponding test file and class names when a source file is renamed — which suggests the mirroring convention is well enough obeyed that reviewers only notice when a rename breaks it.

their_rules.statement: Do not assert on raw log text (`caplog.text`); structured assertions via `caplog` (`"event name" in caplog`, `{"event": ...} in caplog`) are fine and preferred.
their_rules.label: SUPPORTED
their_rules.why: Supported but the review history is stricter than the doc: airflow-r438 as mined rejects the `caplog` fixture for log assertions outright in favour of observable behaviour or a mocked logger, whereas AGENTS.md explicitly blesses structured `caplog` assertions — and candidate airflow-r323 (support 1) even requires that a test taking `caplog` assert on it.

their_rules.statement: Put any files you generate (PR reviews, reports, scratch output) under `files/`, creating it if it does not exist.
their_rules.label: UNSUPPORTED
their_rules.why: No evidence because our corpus cannot see it: agent scratch output never appears in a merged PR diff, so it can never attract a line-level review comment. The nearest visible analogue is candidate airflow-r525 (support 1) on not committing build output.

their_rules.statement: Commit messages and PR titles must not use Conventional Commits prefixes (`fix:`, `feat:`, `chore:`); write the subject as plain imperative prose focused on user impact, under 70 chars for the PR title.
their_rules.label: UNSUPPORTED
their_rules.why: No evidence because our corpus cannot see it — we mine line-level review comments on diffs, and commit subjects and PR titles are not diff lines; a `commit-msg` prek hook (`check-no-conventional-commit-message`) plus CI rejects them anyway. The visible analogue is airflow-r431 (support 3), which enforces the identical convention on provider changelog lines, so the convention is real and policed wherever it lands in a diff.

their_rules.statement: The commit message body describes why the change is made — the motivation and context — never what changed.
their_rules.label: UNSUPPORTED
their_rules.why: No evidence because our corpus cannot see commit bodies. Candidate airflow-r652 (support 2) applies the same instinct where it is visible — PR narration and methodology notes do not belong in a changelog or release-note line.

their_rules.statement: Never add a `Co-Authored-By` trailer naming the agent as co-author of a commit.
their_rules.label: UNSUPPORTED
their_rules.why: No evidence because our corpus cannot see it — commit trailers are not diff lines, and the rule is recent enough that it may also predate very few violations.

their_rules.statement: Always push branches to `origin` (the contributor's fork); never push directly to `upstream`, and never directly to `main` on either remote.
their_rules.source: AGENTS.md § Commits and PRs → Git remote naming conventions
their_rules.label: UNSUPPORTED
their_rules.why: No evidence because our corpus cannot see it: this is a process rule about git operations, which leaves no trace in the line-level review comments of a merged PR.

their_rules.statement: Review the full diff and verify every change is intentional and related to the task — remove any unrelated changes before pushing.
their_rules.source: AGENTS.md § Commits and PRs → Creating Pull Requests (self-review step 1)
their_rules.label: SUPPORTED
their_rules.why: Four PRs where reviewers asked for the diff to be pared back to what the title and description claim — stray uv.lock churn from a rebase, an independent schema-fix migration riding along with a feature migration, a second unrelated feature.

their_rules.statement: `uv.lock` is generated by `uv lock`/`uv sync` and committed; on a conflict delete it and regenerate rather than hand-resolving.
their_rules.label: SUPPORTED
their_rules.why: Review history goes one step further than the doc: regenerating is not enough — airflow-r420 requires the lock to be regenerated against fresh main so it carries only the dependency changes this PR actually makes, since a stale-base regeneration silently adds extras or drops dependencies.

their_rules.statement: A PR that ships a workaround, version cap, mitigation or partial fix must open a GitHub tracking issue, reference it by number in the PR body, and add the full issue URL as a comment at the workaround site in the code — never vague forward-looking phrases like "will open a tracking issue".
their_rules.source: AGENTS.md § Commits and PRs → Tracking issues for deferred work
their_rules.label: SUPPORTED
their_rules.why: Relied on .bob/rules/airflow-candidates.md, and the convergence is striking for below-threshold patterns: airflow-r733 (support 2) requires a dependency cap to carry a comment naming the upstream issue and the lift condition, airflow-r747 (support 2) requires every version-compat shim to name the exact release or a removal TODO, and airflow-r524 (support 1) the same for trigger backward-compat fallbacks. Three independent candidates asking for the same comment-at-the-workaround-site discipline is strong support that the promotion threshold happened to split across surfaces.

their_rules.statement: Anything an agent drafts that is posted to GitHub (PR/issue comments, reviews, line-level review comments) must end with a `Drafted-by:` attribution footer.
their_rules.source: AGENTS.md § Commits and PRs → GitHub messages drafted by agents
their_rules.label: UNSUPPORTED
their_rules.why: No evidence because our corpus cannot see it — we mine the content of review comments, not their authorship footers, and this convention is new enough that the mined PR range largely predates it.

their_rules.statement: AI agents must not mention or tag individual contributors with GitHub usernames unless explicitly instructed; refer to roles, teams, code ownership or components instead.
their_rules.source: AGENTS.md § Commits and PRs → Do not tag individuals
their_rules.label: UNSUPPORTED
their_rules.why: No evidence because our corpus cannot see it: this constrains what an agent writes into a comment, and the mined rules describe code expectations extracted from those comments, not the comments' social conventions.

their_rules.statement: Never edit generated files by hand when a generation workflow exists.
their_rules.label: SUPPORTED
their_rules.why: airflow-r421 (support 3) names the concrete instances reviewers caught — hand-edited `get_provider_info.py`, hand-edited task-SDK `_generated.py`, and a `provider.yaml` change without the regenerated output — with candidate airflow-r484 (support 1) adding the UI `openapi-gen/` client.

their_rules.statement: Never commit secrets, credentials, or tokens.
their_rules.label: UNSUPPORTED
their_rules.why: No mined rule, and this looks like the well-obeyed-plus-tooling case: secret scanning and maintainer diff review before CI approval (contributing-docs/05_pull_requests.rst on suspicious changes) catch it upstream of line comments. The corpus polices the neighbouring leak instead — candidate airflow-r774 (support 2) forbids logging a Connection, `get_uri()` output or any credential-bearing string.
